introHtml:
If you're hunting for a pipe fence builder in Waco TX, you want a crew that's worked cattle, not just set posts. Brazos Ridge Fence Co. builds welded 2-3/8 inch drill-stem pipe fence for ranches across McLennan, Bosque, and Falls counties, and we build it to take a hit from a 1,400 pound bull and stay standing. Most pipe fence around here runs $12 to $28 per linear foot depending on rail count, gates, and how rocky your ground is.

We also hang cattle-tight net wire at $3.50 to $8 per foot, and we build corrals and working pens that move cattle the way cattle actually move. If you're still comparing options, our ranch fence cost guide lays out real numbers side by side, and barbed wire is there when the budget calls for it. Call (509) 351-8404 and we'll walk your fence line with you.

sections.heading: What Pipe Fence Costs in Waco and Central Texas
sections.html:
Welded drill-stem pipe fence runs $12 to $28 per linear foot in the Waco area. Where you land in that range comes down to rail count, corner and gate work, and terrain. Here's how it usually shakes out:

  • 2-rail pipe fence: $12 to $16 per foot. Good for perimeter lines and horse pastures.
  • 3-rail pipe fence: $16 to $22 per foot. The standard for cattle on most ranches around here.
  • 4-rail and heavy corral fence: $22 to $28 per foot. Built for bulls, pens, and high-pressure spots.
  • Add cattle-tight net wire: $3.50 to $8 per foot on top, depending on wire gauge and height.

Rocky ground near Crawford or Valley Mills adds drilling time, and long straight runs bring the per-foot price down. For the full breakdown across every fence type, see our ranch fence cost guide, or call (509) 351-8404 for a free written estimate on your exact acreage.

sections.heading: Corrals, Working Pens, and Cattle-Tight Combos
sections.html:
A pasture fence keeps cattle in. A working pen has to hold them when they're stirred up and pushing, which is a different job entirely. We build corrals, sorting pens, alleys, and crowding areas from welded drill stem, sized for your herd and your chute setup.

Good pen design saves you help on working days. We lay out gates so one person can sort, set alley widths so cattle keep moving forward, and put the heaviest pipe where animals bunch up. If your current pens were cobbled together over 30 years, we can rework them in phases so you're never without a place to work cattle.

For pastures running calves, goats, or sheep, we hang net wire under a pipe top rail. You get the visibility and strength of pipe up top and a cattle-tight barrier down low for $3.50 to $8 per foot. It's the same idea behind our game fencing, just built for stock instead of whitetail.

sections.heading: Pipe vs Wood: Why Ranchers Around Waco Switch
sections.html:
Wood fence looks good the day it goes in. Then Central Texas gets to work on it. Blackland clay swells and shrinks with every wet spring and dry summer, posts rot at the ground line, and a 1,200 pound cow scratching herself will loosen a wood post in one season.

Here's the honest comparison from a crew that builds both:

  • Lifespan: welded pipe goes 40 to 50 years. Wood posts around here give you 15 to 20 before you're replacing them one by one.
  • Upkeep: pipe needs paint every decade or so. Wood needs constant post swaps, re-nailing, and staining.
  • Strength: drill stem shrugs off cattle pressure, feed trucks backing up, and storm-thrown limbs.
  • Cost over time: pipe costs more per foot up front, but spread over its life it's usually the cheaper fence you'll ever build.

That's why so much of our corral and entrance gate work is tear-out jobs, pulling rotted wood and replacing it with pipe that the next owner won't have to touch.

faq.q: How much does pipe fence cost per foot in Waco?
faq.a: Welded 2-3/8 inch drill-stem pipe fence runs $12 to $28 per linear foot in the Waco area. A 2-rail perimeter fence sits at the low end around $12 to $16, a standard 3-rail cattle fence runs $16 to $22, and heavy 4-rail corral fence runs $22 to $28. Rocky ground, extra gates, and short broken-up runs push the price up. Call (509) 351-8404 and we'll put an exact number in writing for free.

faq.q: How long does a pipe fence last compared to wood?
faq.a: A welded drill-stem pipe fence lasts 40 to 50 years with little more than an occasional coat of paint. Wood posts in Central Texas clay typically rot out in 15 to 20 years, and you're usually replacing individual posts well before that. Over the life of the fence, pipe almost always costs less per year than wood.

faq.q: Can you add cattle-tight net wire to a pipe fence?
faq.a: Yes, and it's one of our most requested combos. Net wire runs $3.50 to $8 per foot depending on wire gauge and height, hung under a pipe top rail. That setup holds calves, goats, and sheep that would slip through barbed wire, while the pipe carries the strength up top.

faq.q: Do you build corrals and working pens?
faq.a: We do, and it's some of our favorite work. We build sorting pens, alleys, crowding areas, and full working facilities from welded drill stem, usually at $22 to $28 per foot for the heavy sections. We lay out gates and alley widths so one or two people can work cattle without a fight. Pen rebuilds can be phased so you always have a working area available.

faq.q: What if a storm knocks down my fence or my cattle get out?
faq.a: Call (509) 351-8404 any hour. We run a 24/7 emergency line for storm damage and cattle-out situations across McLennan, Bosque, and Falls counties. We'll get a temporary patch in fast to contain your stock, then give you a free written estimate on the permanent repair.
